key_terms.meaning: A load whose line of action misses the centroid of the joint or bolt group by a distance e, so it causes both direct force and moment.
The area centre of the bolt cross-sections; the eccentric moment F·e is taken about this point.
F/n, where F is the total load in N and n is the number of bolts; it acts parallel to the load.
F·e·r/Σr², where r is the bolt's distance from the centroid in mm; it acts perpendicular to r.
0.707t for a 90° fillet weld of leg size t; the weakest plane of the weld, area = throat × length.
J = Σ(A·r² + I_self) about the weld-group centroid; torsional shear is T·r/J.
Actual run of weld minus an allowance for start and stop craters at the two ends.
A pin or cotter loaded across two cross-sections, so each section carries half the load: τ = P/(2A).
tan λ = l/(π·d_m), where l = lead in mm and d_m = mean thread diameter in mm.
T = (W·d_m/2)·(μ + tan λ)/(1 − μ·tan λ) for a square thread, W = load in N, μ = thread friction coefficient.
One that holds the load when the effort is removed, that is μ ≥ tan λ, or friction angle φ ≥ λ.
η = tan λ / tan(λ + φ); the fraction of input work that raises the load.
C = D/d, the ratio of mean coil diameter D to wire diameter d; usual range 4 to 12.
K_w = (4C−1)/(4C−4) + 0.615/C; correction for direct shear and wire curvature, so τ_max = K_w·8WD/(πd³).
δ = 8WD³n/(Gd⁴), where n = active coils and G = shear modulus in N/mm².
Resonance of the spring coils when a disturbing frequency equals the spring's natural frequency, giving violent stress waves.
Two springs, one inside the other, of different wire size but equal free length, sharing load at equal deflection.
τ_a/τ_e + τ_m/τ_u = 1, with τ_a = alternating shear, τ_m = mean shear, τ_e = endurance limit, τ_u = ultimate shear strength.
A leaf shorter than the master leaf; stacking leaves of decreasing length makes the spring a beam of near-constant strength.
C_s = (ω₁ − ω₂)/ω, where ω₁ and ω₂ are the maximum and minimum speeds in rad/s and ω is the mean speed.
σ = ρv², where ρ = density in kg/m³ and v = rim speed in m/s; it sets the upper speed of a rimmed flywheel.

takeaways: An eccentric load is handled by splitting it into a direct share for every fastener plus a moment share proportional to distance from the centroid, then adding the two as vectors at the worst point.
A weld carries load only through its throat; bending and torsion of the weld group are found from its second moment about the group centroid.
Knuckle and cotter joints are designed part by part, each part checked for its own failure mode: tension, shear, bearing or crushing.
A power screw is an inclined plane on a cylinder: torque must beat thread friction, and the same lead angle and friction decide both efficiency and self-locking.
Spring wire carries torsion, not tension; the curvature correction gives the real maximum shear at the inside of the coil.
Surge is a resonance problem, cured by changing the spring's natural frequency, not by adding material.
Concentric springs share load in the ratio of their stiffnesses, because they must deflect equally.
Fatigue design of a spring replaces one static stress by a mean and an alternating shear compared against an endurance limit.
A laminated leaf spring is a constant-strength beam, so stress and deflection both fall as the number of leaves rises.
A flywheel stores energy as rotating inertia: the allowable speed fluctuation fixes the inertia, and rim centrifugal stress fixes the top speed.
bank_note: Long answers in this unit usually want a labelled sketch, the free-body split into direct and moment effects, and a final numeric check of the worst point against an allowable stress.

bank.q: Explain how an eccentric load on a bolt group is resolved into a direct share and a moment share, and derive the expression for the moment shear on any bolt.
outline: Locate the centroid of the bolt group
Direct shear F/n on every bolt, parallel to the load
Moment M = F·e about the centroid
Assume the plate rotates rigidly: force proportional to radius r
M = Σ(F_i·r_i) = k·Σr_i², so F_i = F·e·r_i/Σr_i²
Direction perpendicular to r_i; vector sum at the worst bolt

bank.q: Sketch a knuckle joint and a cotter joint, name every part, and state the failure mode each part is designed against.
outline: Knuckle: eye, fork, pin, collar; pin in double shear and bearing
Eye in tension across the net section and in crushing
Fork in tension and in crushing
Cotter: socket, spigot, cotter; cotter in double shear and crushing
Rod in tension, rod end in tearing, collar in crushing
State the design equation for each mode

bank.q: Define lead, pitch, thread angle and lead angle of a power screw. Show that a square-threaded screw is self-locking when μ ≥ tan λ.
outline: Unwrap one turn of the thread as an inclined plane
tan λ = l/(π d_m)
Friction angle φ = tan⁻¹μ
Torque expression and its sign when lowering the load
Load holds when the lowering torque is zero or negative
Condition μ ≥ tan λ, independent of load

bank.q: Explain surge in a helical compression spring: its cause, its effect on stress, and the standard ways of preventing it.
outline: Coils behave as a spring-mass system with a natural frequency
Resonance when disturbing frequency matches it, or a harmonic of it
Large stress waves, noise, early failure
Raise natural frequency by stiffer or lighter spring, or fewer active coils
Use of damping, nested springs or a damper friction device
Keep natural frequency well above the operating frequency

bank.q: Describe a laminated leaf spring with a neat sketch and explain why it is called a beam of constant strength.
outline: Master leaf with eyes, graduated leaves, centre clamp, rebound clips
Bending moment falls from the centre towards the tips
Leaf length reduced as moment falls, so section modulus falls in proportion
Stress therefore nearly the same in every leaf
Uniform strength beam saves material compared with a plain plate
Nip and pre-stress mentioned

bank.q: A bracket carries 12 kN at 250 mm from the centroid of a group of six bolts lying on a circle of 200 mm diameter. Find the size of the bolts if the allowable shear stress is 60 N/mm².
outline: Direct shear = F/n on each bolt
Σr² with r = 100 mm for all six bolts
Moment shear = F·e·r/Σr², perpendicular to r
Vector sum, taking the angle between the two components
d from τ = F_max/(π d²/4), round up to a standard size

bank.q: A bracket is welded to a column by fillet welds and carries an eccentric load. Show how you would size the weld, combining direct, bending and torsional shear at the critical point.
outline: Throat = 0.707 × leg size
Weld treated as a line, then multiplied by throat for area and second moment
Direct shear = P/A
Bending shear = M·y/I about the axis of bending
Torsional shear = T·r/J about the centroid
Vector sum at the farthest point, compare with allowable weld shear

bank.q: A single-start square-threaded power screw of 40 mm nominal diameter and 7 mm pitch raises a load of 15 kN. Taking μ = 0.12, find the torque required, the efficiency, and check self-locking.
outline: tan λ = l/(π d_m) with l = 7 mm
Torque T = (W d_m/2)(μ + tan λ)/(1 − μ tan λ)
Collar friction torque added if a collar is given
η = tan λ / tan(λ + φ)
Compare μ with tan λ to confirm self-locking

bank.q: Design a helical compression spring to carry a load fluctuating between 300 N and 900 N over 10⁶ cycles, with a spring index of 6 and a known endurance limit. State every check you would make.
outline: Choose wire diameter from Wahl-corrected maximum shear
Compute τ_max = K_w·8WD/(πd³) at the solid length and at the working load
Split into τ_m and τ_a, apply Goodman or Soderberg with the corrected endurance limit
Compute deflection δ = 8WD³n/(Gd⁴) and check the stiffness needed
Check solid length, clash allowance, buckling and surge frequency
Specify material, end condition and surface treatment

bank.q: Two concentric springs, outer index 8 and inner index 6, must together carry 5 kN at equal deflection. Determine how the load is shared and how the solid lengths must be set.
outline: Equal deflection means equal axial travel
Stiffness k = Gd⁴/(8D³n)
Load ratio = stiffness ratio
Check that inner spring fits inside outer with radial clearance
Choose a clearance so the springs do not touch when compressed

bank.q: A rimmed flywheel runs at a mean speed of 300 rpm with a coefficient of speed fluctuation of 0.02 and must absorb 15 kJ per cycle. Find the required inertia and check the centrifugal stress in a cast-iron rim.
outline: ΔE = I·ω²·C_s, so I = ΔE/(ω²C_s)
Rim mass from I ≈ m·r² for a thin rim
Rim speed v = πDN/60
σ = ρv²; compare with allowable for cast iron
Comment on arm stress and on limiting speed

bank.q: A light bracket must be fixed to a frame and carries an eccentric load. Compare a bolted joint and a welded joint for this duty, covering load path, stress analysis and practical choice.
outline: Bolted: direct plus moment shear, bearing on the plate, slip and pre-load
Welded: throat area, bending and torsion of the weld group
Detailing: edge distance versus weld access and distortion
Fatigue: welds have poorer fatigue strength, bolts are easier to inspect
Assembly, dismantling and repair
Recommendation with reasons

bank.q: A vehicle suspension can use a helical spring or a laminated leaf spring. Evaluate the two for stiffness, load sharing, space and failure behaviour, and justify the usual choice for a light commercial vehicle.
outline: Helical: torsion of wire, compact, stores more energy per unit mass
Leaf: bending of strips, acts as beam and locates the axle
Constant-strength action of graduated leaves, friction damping between leaves
Load sharing and progressive stiffening
Failure: leaf gives warning and retains some load path, coil collapses
Choice justified with cost and maintenance

bank.q: A power screw in a screw jack wears out quickly and also backs down under load. Analyse the likely reasons and propose design changes.
outline: Low efficiency means a large friction angle relative to lead angle
Bearing pressure on the threads too high: increase thread area or add a collar bearing
Poor lubrication and material pairing
Backing down means μ < tan λ: reduce lead or increase friction deliberately
Check buckling of the screw and nut height
Trade-off between efficiency and self-locking stated clearly

glossary.def: The axial distance between corresponding points on adjacent threads, in mm.
The axial distance the nut travels in one full turn of the screw, equal to pitch times the number of starts.
The average of the major and minor diameters, d_m = d − p/2 for a square thread; used in all torque formulas.
φ = tan⁻¹μ, the angle whose tangent is the coefficient of friction.
Torque lost at the thrust collar, T_c = μ_c·W·(r_o + r_i)/2, where r_o and r_i are the collar radii in mm.
Compressive stress on a projected area, such as p = P/(d·t) on a pin or p = W/(π d_m·n_t·h) on a thread.
Tensile failure of a member across its net section, as at the eye of a knuckle joint.
Local compressive failure where two parts press against each other, checked on the projected contact area.
A triangular weld joining two surfaces at right angles; load is carried on its throat, not on the leg.
A weld across the full thickness of the joined plates; the throat equals the plate thickness.
The coils of a spring that deflect; end coils that only seat do not count.
Length of a compression spring with all coils touching, L_s = n_t·d, where n_t is the total number of coils.
Stiffness k = W/δ, the load per unit deflection in N/mm.
The axial length of a compression spring with no load applied.
The stress amplitude a material survives for a very large number of cycles without fatigue failure.
σ_m = (σ_max + σ_min)/2 and σ_a = (σ_max − σ_min)/2, the steady and cyclic parts of a stress.
The small initial gap given between leaves of a leaf spring so that they share load evenly after assembly.
The longest, full-length leaf of a laminated spring, whose ends carry the eyes.
The reciprocal of the coefficient of speed fluctuation, m = 1/C_s.
Tensile stress around the rim caused by its own centrifugal force at speed.
